title: Industrial Activity: Machinery, High-Tech and Process

questions.q: In "Who needs this, and who is your first user Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Check sheet: of 40 defects, 22 are drill misalignment, 10 burrs, 8 other. Fix the largest first: a simple jig.
Write a one-page idea: who, what you will do, what success looks like in numbers.
Propose one fix for each with an expected saving in minutes or currency.
Quality tools: a check sheet to count defects, a bar chart ordered by size to show the biggest cause, and the five whys to find the root of a problem.

questions.q: In "Kick-off circle Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Agree which data you must still collect.
Peers ask three questions: who is it for, why you, what could go wrong.
Process: cut 4 min, drill 3 min, assemble 6 min, pack 2 min = 15 min of work per unit, but units wait 20 min before assembly. Waiting is the largest waste.

questions.q: In "Start the practice task Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Find the three biggest waste points: waiting, rework, motion, over-production, scrap, stoppages.
Write the machine's weekly preventive-maintenance checklist: look, listen, clean, lubricate, tighten, record.
Each learner reads their idea aloud (3 minutes).
Measure the result against your goal: minutes per unit, scrap percent, stoppage hours per week, output per shift.
